I was inspired by a clever guy in another thread to do a rough calculation. It blew my mind.

the combined liquid fuels from an average barrel of crude oil will produce a minimum of 317kg of CO2 when consumed (http://numero57.net/2008/03/20/carbon-dioxide-emissions-per-barrel-of-crude/)

Assuming the unit of a barrel of oil, then every barrel on earth is capable of producing on average 317 kg of CO2.

The Organization for Petroleum Exporting Countries reports that there are 1.5 trillion barrels of crude oil reserves left in the world (https://www.seeker.com/how-much-oil-is-left-on-earth-1792718444.html)

1.5e12 barrels * 317 kg CO2/barrel = 4.755e14 kg CO2

The atmosphere has a mass of about 5.15e18 kg (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Earth#cite_note-9)

So dividing our minimum mass of CO2 from burning every barrel of oil on earth by the mass of earth's atmosphere:

4.755e14 / 5.15e18 = 9.2 e -5

So all of the CO2 from burning all oil on earth (at once) would be roughly 92 ppm when added to earth's atmosphere. Basically we'd see the total CO2 go from the current 415 ppm to somewhere between 500 and 600 ppm.

I didn't account for the already existing CO2 in the atmosphere, because it is completely negligible at these orders of magnitude.
